title: Provisioning: improve operator-facing errors for DNS/TLS, GPU health, and quota failures
author: Gabe Wilson
release_notes:
- Operator-facing provisioning failures now include actionable remediations + runbook links for common DNS/TLS, GPU health, and quota issues.
- Provisioning events include a stable error_code for alert routing and dashboard grouping.
description: Problem: during the pilot we were surfacing raw provider/cluster errors (e.g., kubelet TLS failures, transient DNS resolution errors, NVML/ECC flags, and cloud quota errors) directly to operators via the provisioning run status + CLI output. This caused slow triage and inconsistent actions across Infra/SRE, and made it hard to build reliable alerting on failure types. This PR adds (1) a normalized error taxonomy (error_code + category) for the most common provisioning failure modes we hit in Week 2/3, (2) friendlier operator messages with the next 1-3 concrete checks to run, and (3) consistent pointers to the right runbook sections (Confluence) so the bot/CLI/control plane all point to the same place. Scope: DNS/TLS failures (in-cluster and external resolution, cert SAN mismatches), GPU health failures (ECC, NVML init, driver mismatch), and quota failures (insufficient regional quota / instance capacity). Non-goals: changing readiness gate logic or adding new gates; this is purely message+classification and plumbing. Notes: includes cardinality safeguards (error_code is low-cardinality; raw provider errors remain in debug_details but are not used for metrics labels). Screenshots/Examples: CLI now prints a short summary plus a “Next steps” block and a Runbook URL; control plane API returns error_code and runbook_url in the stage failure payload; Slack bot picks up error_code for routing. Test plan: unit tests for classification mapping; integration test for a simulated DNS failure and a simulated quota failure; manual run in staging by forcing an invalid resolver and by toggling an IAM policy to provoke quota-like provider errors. Follow-ups: extend taxonomy to helm bootstrap misconfigurations once ENG-2742/ENG-2746 stabilize and we have more pilot data.
commits: provisioning/errors: add ProvisioningErrorCode + category mapping (dns_tls, gpu_health, quota)
control-plane: include error_code, operator_message, runbook_url in stage failure payloads
cli: render actionable Next steps block and link to runbook section anchors
events: emit provisioning.failure with normalized error_code (low-cardinality) and attach debug_details separately
tests: add unit coverage for classifier + golden output snapshots for CLI rendering
notable_snippet:
Example (CLI output)
Stage: Validating
Result: FAILED (GPU_HEALTH_ECC)
Summary: One or more nodes reported uncorrectable ECC errors during GPU health validation.
Next steps:
1) Check node dmesg for Xid/ECC events and confirm this is not a transient reset.
2) Drain + replace affected nodes (auto-replace is safe at this stage; pool is not in routing).
3) Re-run validation only: redwoodctl provision rerun --stage validating --pool <pool-id>
Runbook: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGINFRA/Dedicated+pool+provisioning+runbook#Dedicatedpoolprovisioningrunbook-GPUhealthcheck(ECC/NVML)
review_conversation: Rafael Mendes: Can we guarantee error_code stays low-cardinality? We should not tag raw cloud provider messages in metrics labels. Also please ensure operator_message is safe to show in Slack (no secrets/tokens).

Gabe Wilson (author): Yep. error_code is an enum with ~14 values in this PR. Raw provider errors go into debug_details and are excluded from metrics labels; Slack uses error_code + sanitized operator_message only. Added a redaction step for any strings matching common token patterns before rendering.

Victor Alvarez: For DNS/TLS, can we distinguish between (a) node can’t resolve cluster DNS, (b) control plane can’t reach node due to TLS SAN mismatch, and (c) external egress DNS failures? The remediation differs.

Gabe Wilson (author): Added three distinct codes: DNS_CLUSTER_RESOLUTION, DNS_EXTERNAL_EGRESS, TLS_CERT_SAN_MISMATCH. Classifier checks the failing probe + error substrings (x509 + SAN) and falls back to DNS_UNKNOWN when ambiguous. Added tests for the x509 branch.

Kira Thompson: Runbook links look good, but please anchor them to sections we control. The current URLs in code point to a draft page title; prefer stable page IDs or a link index so we can update without code changes.

Gabe Wilson (author): Good call. Replaced hard-coded links with runbooks/links/runbook_index.go (keyed by error_code). We can update that mapping independently and keep anchors stable; also added a doc comment with the Confluence page IDs.

Allison Grant: Metrics naming: please align with PR-48239 naming (provisioning_failure_total{error_code=...}). Also, ensure we don’t emit both category and error_code as separate labels on the same metric to avoid combinatorial explosion.
Gabe Wilson (author): Updated to match provisioning_failure_total with only error_code label. category remains in structured event payload only (not on metrics).

Rafael Mendes: One more thing: quota errors are often intermittent capacity rather than actual quota. Can we present operator_message without claiming it’s quota unless we’re sure? We’ve been bitten by confusing messaging.

Gabe Wilson (author): Adjusted messaging: QUOTA_INSUFFICIENT is only used when the provider error explicitly includes quota exceeded; otherwise we use CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE with guidance to try alternate AZ / waitlist / rerun. Added test vectors for both.
Rafael Mendes: Approved after the runbook link indirection + metric label changes. Thanks.
Victor Alvarez: Approved. DNS/TLS separation will help oncall.
Kira Thompson: Approved. Please ping me when we update the runbook anchors post-merge.
